aboutH2: Pine River Institute: Live-In Treatment for Youth 13 to 19 near Shelburne, Ontario
intro: Pine River Institute is a not-for-profit, live-in treatment centre for young people aged 13 to 19 who are struggling with addictive behaviours, and often with other mental health problems as well. The campus sits on 200 acres just outside Shelburne, in the Township of Mulmur, roughly 100 km northwest of Toronto. The program opened in 2006 and is run as a registered charity.

Most families come to Pine River after other help has not worked. The centre says the teens it sees are usually struggling on several fronts at once: substance use, self-harm or disordered eating, anxiety or depression, school refusal or expulsion, running away, trouble with the law, or trauma. Many have already tried outpatient therapy, day treatment or a short residential stay.

pillars.title: A 200-Acre Campus in Mulmur, Outside Shelburne
pillars.body: After the wilderness phase, students live on Pine River's campus on River Road in Mulmur, a few minutes from Shelburne in Dufferin County. The land was once the Toronto District School Board's Pine River Outdoor Education Centre. Pine River leased it from 2006 and bought it in 2014. Moffat House, opened in 2021, added 24 beds, and the Neal Hall dining hall was refurbished in 2023 so everyone can eat together. There is a gym, an outdoor basketball court, volleyball, a large playing field and trails used for hiking and cross-country skiing. Each spring students help tap the sugar maples and boil sap in the sugar shack.

pillars.title: Teens Keep Earning Credits While Parents Do Their Own Work
pillars.body: A typical campus day has two to three hours of class, two hours of physical activity, two hours of group therapy and an hour of art, music or drama, plus chores and free time. Teachers come from the Upper Grand District School Board and plan each student's courses with the clinical team, so credits keep adding up. Parents have work of their own, too. Pine River expects them to join family therapy, a family group every other Sunday, a parent group every two weeks, a parent retreat and two-day workshops twice a year. Families who live far away can join by phone or video.

pillars.title: A Gradual Return Home, Then Up to a Year of Aftercare
pillars.body: Nobody goes straight from campus back to ordinary life. In the transition phase a student might spend weekdays on campus and weekends at home, or the reverse, while the family writes a home agreement and an Aftercare Plan. Lang House, opened in 2022, gives students finishing the program a place to build new routines before they go home. Aftercare then runs three to 12 months, with individual, group and family therapy and weekly groups for both students and parents. It ends with a graduation on campus.

overview: Pine River's treatment model is based on John McKinnon's Maturity Model. The idea is that addiction in teens is usually a symptom of something underneath, and that delayed maturity leads young people to cope in ways that hurt them. The program works on emotional regulation, empathy, and a realistic sense of the future, inside a structured peer community with clear limits. Intake is continuous, and the program runs 24 hours a day, every day of the year.

afterOverview: Pine River tracks its own results. In parent reports for families who finished treatment, 57% of youth were using substances daily before Pine River, compared with 10% one to two years after. School attendance rose from 42% to 96% over the same period. In 2016 the program became the only Canadian program named a Research Designated Program by the National Association of Therapeutic Schools and Programs. Pine River also runs BRANCH, a separate 16-week outpatient program in Toronto for youth referred by partner hospitals.

location.heading: Pine River Institute in Mulmur, Ontario
location.intro: Pine River's campus is on River Road in the Township of Mulmur, a few minutes outside Shelburne in Dufferin County and about an hour and a half north of Toronto by car. Orangeville is about 30 minutes away, Brampton a little over an hour, and Barrie and Collingwood about an hour each, while the first phase of the program takes place in Algonquin Park.

faqIntro: Answers come from Pine River Institute's own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: Who is Pine River Institute for?
faqs.a: Pine River is for young people aged 13 to 19 with addictive behaviours, usually alongside other mental health issues such as anxiety, depression, self-harm or trauma. Most have already tried less intensive help, like outpatient therapy or day treatment, without enough progress. The admissions team decides with each family whether the program is the right fit.

faqs.q: How much does Pine River Institute cost?
faqs.a: For an Ontario teen who qualifies for a Ministry of Health funded bed, the family pays $325 a month plus a $1,000 damage deposit and trust account at admission. Private-pay beds cost $475 a day, with $17,750 due at admission. Aftercare is $325 a month, and the centre offers bursaries to families who cannot afford the fees.

faqs.q: Is Pine River funded by the Ontario government?
faqs.a: Partly. Pine River describes itself as a not-for-profit, fee-for-service program that receives funding support from the Ontario Ministry of Health. The Ministry funds beds for Ontario adolescents who qualify, and families cover a monthly fee for things like parent retreats, transportation and activities. A limited number of beds are not Ministry funded and are paid privately.

faqs.q: How long does the program last?
faqs.a: There is no set length of stay, and Pine River says the average is 12 to 14 months. Students move through the four phases when they show they are ready, not after a fixed number of days. Aftercare at home then lasts from three to 12 months, depending on the family.

faqs.q: What is the Outdoor Leadership Experience?
faqs.a: It is the first phase of the program, six to eight weeks on the land in Algonquin Park. Groups of up to eight students and three staff canoe, hike or snowshoe, and do group work, individual therapy and journaling. After that, students move to the residence on the Shelburne-area campus.

faqs.q: Will my child keep up with school?
faqs.a: Yes. Certified teachers and an educational assistant from the Upper Grand District School Board teach on campus, and every teacher holds special education qualifications. Each student gets an academic plan, and most work toward an Ontario Secondary School Diploma or Certificate, while some take online post-secondary courses.

Parents are expected to take an active part. That means regular family therapy and progress meetings, a family group every other Sunday, a parent group every two weeks in the evening, a parent retreat and two-day parent workshops twice a year. Families who live far away can join by phone or video, and each family has a private Family Bridge website to stay in touch.

faqs.q: Where is Pine River Institute and how far is it from Toronto?
faqs.a: The campus is at 606060 River Road in Mulmur, just outside Shelburne in Dufferin County, about an hour and a half north of Toronto by car. Orangeville is about half an hour away, and Barrie and Collingwood are each about an hour. The head office is in downtown Toronto at 180 Dundas Street West, Suite 1410.

faqs.q: Does Pine River Institute offer detox?
faqs.a: Pine River does not list medical detox among its services, and its recovery.com profile marks detox as not offered. The program is long-term residential treatment for teens. If your child may need medical withdrawal care first, ask the admissions team how they handle it before admission.

faqs.q: How do we apply, and is there a wait?
faqs.a: Start with the online initial screener on Pine River's website, which takes about 10 minutes, or call admissions at 519-925-9225 ext. 139. If the fit looks right, you send supporting documents, your family may be placed on a wait list, and you visit the campus for an assessment before admission. The centre says the wait list can be months long, so it runs a six-week online support program for caregivers who are waiting.

faqs.q: What happens after my child leaves campus?
faqs.a: Students and families build an Aftercare Plan during the transition phase, then continue with aftercare at home for three to 12 months. It includes individual, group and family therapy, weekly groups for students and for parents, and coaching. Aftercare ends with a graduation on campus.
